source_text: Solent quidem isti infirmiores etiam de quibusdam personis ab haeresi captis aedificari in ruinam. Quare illa vel ille fidelisimi et prudentissimi et usitatissimi in ecclesia in illam partem transierunt? Quis hoc dicens non ipse sibi respondet neque prudentes neque fideles neque usitatos aestimandos quos haereses potuerint demutare? Et hoc mirum, opinor, ut probatus aliqui retro postea excidat? Saul, bonus prae ceteris, livore postea evertitur. David, vir bonus secundum cor domini, postea caedis et stupri reus est. Solomon, omni gratia et sapientia donatus a domino, ad idololatriam a mulieribus inducitur. Soli enim dei filio servabatur sine delicto permanere. Quid ergo, si episcopus, si diaconus, si vidua, si virgo, si doctor, si etiam martyr lapsus a regula fuerit, ideo haereses veritatem videbuntur obtinere? Ex personis probamus fidem, an ex fide personas? Nemo est sapiens, nemo fidelis, nemo maior, nisi Christianus. Nemo autem Christianus, nisi qui ad finem usque perseveraverit. Tu, ut homo, extrinsecus unumquemque nosti. Putas quod vides. Vides autem, quousque oculos habes. Sed oculi, inquit, domini alti. Homo in faciem, deus in praecordia contemplatur. Et ideo contemplatur et ideo cognoscit dominus qui sunt eius, et plantam, quam non plantavit, eradicat, et de primis novissimos ostendit: et ventilabrum in manu portat ad purgandam aream suam. Avolent quantum volunt paleae levis fidei quocunque adflatu temptationum, eo purior massa frumenti in horrea domini reponetur. Nonne ab ipso domino quidam discentium scandalizati deverterunt? Nec tamen propterea ceteri quoque discedendum a vestigiis eius putaverunt, sed qui scierunt illum vitae esse verbum et a deo venisse, perseveraverunt in comitatu eius usque ad finem, cum illis, si vellent et ipsi discedere, placide obtulisset. Minus est, si et apostolum eius aliqui Phygelus et Hermogenes et Philetus et Hymenaeus reliquerunt: ipse traditor Christi de apostolis fuit. Miramur de ecclesiis eius, si a quibusdam deseruntur, cum ea nos ostendunt Christianos quae patimur ad exemplum ipsius Christi. Ex nobis, inquit, prodierunt, sed non fuerunt ex nobis. Si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum.
thought_title: The fall of prominent persons does not prove heresy true
orientation: Tertullian is answering the objection that some well-known church members have gone over to heresy, and he argues that their lapse proves nothing about the truth of heresies.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed these weaker ones are accustomed to be built up into ruin even from certain persons captured by heresy. Why did that woman or that man, most faithful and most prudent and most experienced in the church, pass over to that side? Who, saying this, does not himself answer himself, that neither prudent nor faithful nor experienced persons are to be judged those whom heresies have been able to change? And is this strange, I think, that someone approved in the past should afterwards fall away? Saul, good beyond the rest, is afterwards overturned by envy. David, a good man according to the heart of the Lord, is afterwards guilty of murder and adultery. Solomon, gifted by the Lord with all grace and wisdom, is led into idolatry by women. For to the Son of God alone was it reserved to remain without fault. What then, if a bishop, if a deacon, if a widow, if a virgin, if a teacher, if even a martyr has slipped from the rule, will heresies therefore seem to possess the truth? Do we prove faith from persons, or persons from faith? No one is wise, no one faithful, no one greater, unless a Christian. But no one is a Christian, unless he who has persevered to the end. You, as a human being, know each person from the outside. You think what you see. But you see only as long as you have eyes. But the eyes of the Lord, he says, are high. Man looks at the face, God looks into the heart. And therefore the Lord knows and therefore recognizes who are his, and the plant which he has not planted he uproots, and he shows the last from among the first: and he carries a winnowing fork in his hand to cleanse his threshing floor. Let the chaff of light faith fly away as much as they wish in whatever blast of temptations, by that much purer will the mass of grain be stored in the barns of the Lord. Did not some of the disciples, scandalized, turn away from the Lord himself? Nor yet for that reason did the rest think that they too must depart from his footsteps, but those who knew that he was the word of life and had come from God persevered in his company to the end, although he had offered them, if they themselves also wished to depart, the opportunity calmly. It is less, if some Phygelus and Hermogenes and Philetus and Hymenaeus abandoned even his apostle: the betrayer of Christ himself was from among the apostles. Do we wonder about his churches, if they are deserted by some, when those things which we suffer show us to be Christians according to the example of Christ himself? From us, he says, they went out, but they were not from us. If they had been from us, they would surely have remained with us.

choices.english: to be built up into ruin
choices.why: Keeps the paradox of 'aedificari' (built up) with 'in ruinam' (into ruin), which is Tertullian's ironic point that the weak are edified toward destruction.
rejected: to be built up for their downfall

choices.why: The superlative of 'usitatus' means well-practiced or experienced in church life, not merely 'customary' or 'ordinary'.

choices.english: a good man according to the heart of the Lord
choices.why: Echoes the biblical description of David (1 Samuel 13:14) while keeping the literal Latin word order and sense.
rejected: a man after God's own heart
a good man after the Lord's heart

choices.why: The glossary term 'regula fidei' is 'rule of faith'; here 'regula' alone refers to that fixed standard, so 'the rule' preserves the technical sense.

choices.english: carries a winnowing fork in his hand
choices.why: Literal rendering of the agricultural implement, matching the biblical image of separating grain from chaff.
rejected: holds a fan in his hand
has a winnowing shovel in hand

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of chaff and the adjective 'levis' (light, weightless) applied to faith, preserving the image of instability.

pass_b_english: These weaker people are also in the habit of being built up into ruin by certain persons who have been captured by heresy. Why, they ask, did that man or that woman, people of the greatest faith, the greatest wisdom, the most experienced in the church, go over to the other side? Whoever says this should answer his own question: those whom heresies have been able to change should not be considered wise, or faithful, or experienced at all.

And is it so surprising, I wonder, that someone once approved should later fall away? Saul, good beyond all others, was afterward overturned by envy. David, a good man according to the heart of the Lord, later became guilty of murder and adultery. Solomon, gifted by the Lord with every grace and wisdom, was led into idolatry by women. Only the Son of God was preserved to remain without fault.

What then? If a bishop, if a deacon, if a widow, if a virgin, if a teacher, if even a martyr has slipped from the rule, will heresies on that account seem to possess the truth? Do we test faith by persons, or persons by faith? No one is wise, no one is faithful, no one is great, unless he is a Christian. And no one is a Christian unless he has persevered to the end.

You, being human, know each person only from the outside. You think what you see is what there is. But you see only as far as your eyes reach. Yet the eyes of the Lord, Scripture says, are high. Man looks at the face, but God looks into the heart. And therefore the Lord knows who are his, and he uproots the plant he did not plant, and he shows the last to be first; and he carries a winnowing fork in his hand to cleanse his threshing floor. Let the chaff of light faith fly wherever it will at every blast of temptation; the purer mass of grain will be stored in the Lord's barns.

Did not some of the Lord's own disciples turn away in scandal? Yet the rest did not think they should therefore abandon his footsteps. Those who knew that he was the word of life and had come from God remained in his company to the end, even though he had calmly offered them the chance to leave as well, if they wished.

It is a smaller matter if some abandoned his apostle: Phygelus and Hermogenes, Philetus and Hymenaeus. The betrayer of Christ himself was one of the apostles. Are we surprised when his churches are deserted by certain people, when the very things we suffer as Christians show us to be following the example of Christ himself? They went out from us, Scripture says, but they were not from us. If they had been from us, they would surely have remained with us (1 John 2:19).

problems.quote: Only the Son of God was kept from remaining without fault.
problems.source_quote: Soli enim dei filio servabatur sine delicto permanere.
problems.why: Reverses the sense; Latin says he was preserved to remain faultless, not prevented from it.
problems.fix: Only the Son of God was preserved to remain without fault.
problems.ruling: Latin 'servabatur sine delicto permanere' means preserved to remain without fault; English 'kept from remaining without fault' reverses the sense.

edits.old: Only the Son of God was kept from remaining without fault.
edits.new: Only the Son of God was preserved to remain without fault.

fixed: Corrected the negation: 'servabatur sine delicto permanere' means he was preserved to remain without fault, not kept from remaining without fault.

last_rejected.quote: Yet the eyes of the Lord, Scripture says, are high.
last_rejected.why: The Latin quote is spoken by the Lord; the English adds “Scripture says,” misattributing the speaker.
last_rejected.fix: Yet the eyes of the Lord, he says, are high.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'inquit' introduces a quotation; 'oculi domini alti' is scriptural (Ps. 10:4), so 'Scripture says' is a reasonable rendering.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker of the opening question, smoothed sentence order, identified the four apostates as those who abandoned Paul's apostle, and removed the em dash while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.quote: Phygelus and Hermogenes and Philetus and Hymenaeus
notes.why: Four names dropped without context; reader cannot tell if these are biblical or historical figures.
notes.fix: Note these are figures mentioned in Paul's letters as deserters or false teachers.
